title: Get back into your account
summary: The list of ways back into an existing account on this phone, from fast to slow (ADR 0057, ADR 0059). The first row is the synced recovery token when this phone has one.

key.description: The row key of registries/onboarding.json recovery.

visible.description: false when its when state does not hold or its gate issue is open.

rows.description: In registries/onboarding.json recovery order. token shows only when a synced recovery token is on the phone (syncedToken). bipe-app shows oldPhone (bipe-chat/bipe#608); the forks keep its planned:203 gate and hide it. apple and google show only when GET /v1/links/providers offers a path for them on this platform (ADR 0096).

hasSyncedToken.description: true when the iCloud Keychain or Block Store holds a recovery token for an account that is not signed in on this phone.

linkProviders.description: Providers with a path on this platform, from GET /v1/links/providers. Empty when the server offers none or does not answer.

appear.effect: Reads the synced store for a recovery token and GET /v1/links/providers, and sets hasSyncedToken, linkProviders and rows.

chooseToken.effect: Opens recovery-pin for the synced token.

chooseOldPhone.effect: Opens recovery-old-phone: the camera scans the code that the old phone shows on link-phone-show (ADR 0059).

chooseBeta.effect: Opens the sign-in for old beta accounts with e-mail and password. Input with @ that is not a Matrix ID (@localpart:server) is an e-mail: POST /v1/beta/login with the e-mail and the password gives the Matrix ID (bipe#627), then Client.login with that Matrix ID and the password. A localpart or a full Matrix ID goes to Client.login as it is. A 401 from /v1/beta/login shows the same text as a failed Client.login, so an unknown e-mail and a wrong password look the same. After sign-in the app moves the account to device-first (POST /v1/me/device-first).

notes: Rows, titles and bodies come from the generated onboarding code (registries/onboarding.json recovery). bipe_recovery_email_body takes recoveryDelayHours.email from registries/accounts.json.
Guardians and CPF are not rows yet: their server paths are not built (Recovery.method guardian and cpf in api/openapi.yaml). Add them as registry rows when they ship.
With two accounts on the phone (ADR 0086), the token row takes the token of an account that is not signed in.
Every path gives access only. Message history needs another device or the recovery key (rule 5); recovery-waiting and encryption-status say so.
Bipe logic: BipeCredentialStore.recoveryToken(excluding:) (iOS), BipeRecoveryTokenStore.recoveryToken and BipeDeviceAccount.hasRecoveryToken (Android), BipeAPIClient.moveToDeviceFirst (iOS).
